title: LumenWave telecom pilot — latency gotchas & integration notes
content:
Context: 2025-02-10 technical sync with LumenWave (Rajesh, Sana). They want a low-latency NLU inference layer for live voice assistants (call-routing, slot extraction, intent detection). This is a user scratchpad capturing the call, observed gotchas, quick mitigation ideas and next steps.

Attendees:
- LumenWave: Rajesh Patel (Eng), Sana Iqbal (PM)
- Redwood: Evelyn Park (solutions), Jordan Li (serving-runtime), Priya Nair (SRE)

Customer goals / SLA targets (stated):
- Interactive span: sub-150ms p95 for single-hop intent detection (short prompt + ~30-80 token decode), target 120ms p95 ideally.
- Throughput: ~400 reqs/sec peak for a single region (Europe), steady 120 rps.
- Data residency: EU only for pilot; must be VPC/private control plane.
- Availability: 99.9% during business hours; fallback to cloud endpoint if on-prem capacity constrained.

Primary constraints / gotchas called out on the call:
1) Short request penalty: They observed that the per-request overhead (TLS, auth, model init) dominates for 20–50 token responses. Cold starts hit them hard when routing across clusters.
   - Note: for short sequences, batching hurts latency unless batching window is tiny; but very small windows reduce batching efficiency.

2) TCP/TLS & gRPC tradeoffs: Their current voice stack pushes events over a long-lived gRPC stream. They asked if Redwood supports gRPC streaming with sticky connections to keep TLS handshake overhead minimal.
   - Our notes: long-lived TLS + HTTP/2 streams recommended; avoid per-request client TLS tear-down.

3) KV cache sticky routing: They have a conversational context pattern (short recent history) where cache hits give big wins. But cache invalidation across primary/standby nodes is a concern for dedicated pools.

4) Quantized model accuracy: They plan to evaluate 7B/13B quantized variants on-prem to meet latency. Concern: small accuracy regressions on entity extraction could break routing.

5) Observability blind spots: They want per-call timing (auth, routing, queue time, token gen time, network RTT) surfaced to their APM. Also per-route p95/p99 and a cold-start tag.

6) Mixed workload interference: Batching big decoding jobs (long transcripts) on the same pool might increase tail latency for short NLU requests. Need isolation (priority queues or separate pools).

Initial quick mitigation ideas (prototype-level):
- Sticky sessions + warm routing: use sticky affinity for conversational users so their KV cache stays hot on the same node/pool. Combine with a small warm pool reserve to absorb new sessions.
- Edge aggregator: run a very small, locally quantized model (7B-8bit) on a colocated on-prem instance for the very low-latency fast path; fallback to larger hosted model for complex cases.
- Prefix caching: precompute static prefixes for common prompts (greetings, short slot templates) and use prefix cache to avoid repeated decoding.
- Minimal batching window for short requests: tune batching by request size class; keep 0–5ms window for short NLU class to avoid latency cliffs.
- Pre-warm on scale events: use pre-warm signals from their call system (scheduled traffic surges) to spin up containers/instances ahead of time.

Model & infra recommendations discussed:
- On-prem: Llama2-13B-8bit (quantized VQ configs) as candidate; evaluate extraction F1 vs baseline. If accuracy drop unacceptable, consider 13B float16 on dedicated small GPU (A10/GPU).
- Hosted fallback: use Redwood hosted small-gpu pool with canary routing based on confidence threshold.
- Routing policy: prioritize local pool, then dedicated reserved capacity, then hosted as last resort. Implement circuit-breaker to avoid cascading latency spikes.

Observability & metrics to capture (customer asked explicitly):
- Per-request: auth_latency, routing_latency, queue_time, model_infer_tokens_ms, first_token_ms, total_tokens, model_variant, node_id, cache_hit(true/false), cold_start(true/false).
- Aggregates: p50/95/99 of first_token_ms and total latency, request rate by model_variant, GPU util, batch sizes distribution.
- Alerts: p95 first_token_ms > 150ms for >5min, cache hit rate < 40% for 15min.

Security / compliance notes:
- EU data residency mandatory for pilot. They want Redwood Private with customer VPC and KMS integration for keys. Need audit logs for all inference requests for first 3 months.

Risks and unanswered questions to follow up:
- How much accuracy loss on quantized 8-bit model for entity extraction? Request: Redwood run eval suite on their slot-extraction test set (we need their seed prompts + labeled test pairs).
- Warm pool sizing: need realistic traffic shape from LumenWave (minute-level qps histogram) to size warm reserve.
- Sticky routing durability: how long can we safely keep affinity? Tradeoff between cache hit rate and load imbalance.
- Network topology: confirm if their on-prem boxes sit behind NAT and whether outgoing TLS to Redwood cloud is allowed for control plane.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Evelyn: Draft pilot plan (infra + model split, SLOs, warm-reserve sizing assumptions) and share v1 to Rajesh by 2025-02-18.
- Jordan: Run quick quantized eval of candidate 13B-8bit on Redwood eval harness using their sample slot-extraction dataset (need dataset). Target results summary by 2025-02-20.
- Priya: Prototype minimal observability schema (logs + metrics mapping) and a Grafana dashboard layout; share by 2025-02-19.
- Rajesh (LumenWave): Provide 1 week of minute-level qps hist + representative prompt set + labeled eval pairs (anonymized) by 2025-02-17.
- All: Confirm compliance/legal checklist for EU data residency and audit logging by 2025-02-21 (legal loop-in needed).

Notes to self (quick internal reminders):
- Emphasize small-window batching config in proposal — operationally it's the lever with biggest tail impact.
- Propose a mixed-pool approach: tiny on-prem model for 99% fast path, hosted for 1% heavy inference. Show cost delta vs dedicated-only.
- Need to check whether our Private control plane supports long-lived gRPC streams with TLS passthrough for their stack; escalate to infra if not supported.

Questions for next call with LumenWave:
1) Can they share the anonymized eval set this week? We'll run quantized vs float evals and present numbers.
2) Are there predictable daily surge windows where pre-warms can be scheduled?
3) What is their acceptable degradation for extraction (F1 drop) in exchange for 2x latency improvement?

Meeting artifacts to attach to pilot deck: places to add slides:
- Latency anatomy (auth/routing/queue/infer) and where Redwood gains apply
- Proposed hybrid architecture diagram (on-prem fast path + hosted fallback)
- Cost comparison: dedicated capacity vs hybrid on-prem + hosted fallback

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a short proposal once quant evals return.
